clues.title: Plate: fully white, black text
text: Russian licence plates are **fully white** with black text.
NOTE: Most European counterparts will feature a blue strip on the left hand side.
clues.summary: Fully white plates with black text and no blue strip on the left like most of Europe.

clues.title: Language: Cyrillic with Ы, Э, Ё, Ъ
text: The Russian language uses the **Cyrillic script**, and contains the special letters Ы, Э, Ё and Ъ.
Ё is also used in Mongolian and Ъ is used in Bulgarian.

NOTE: You may rarely come across Russian in both [Ukraine](https://www.google.com/maps/@46.7466337,33.3598742,3a,15y,252.53h,96.14t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1snFUnRbez3yFUVjnKG9azVg!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) and eastern [Estonia](https://www.google.com/maps/@59.3779623,28.1969594,3a,15y,61.93h,93.19t,1.18r/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1sLI0Eu3YxRqFjCr2pUN2tAw!2e0!5s20230901T000000!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).

images.caption: Russian text with the letters Ы Э Ё Ъ shown large

clues.summary: Cyrillic script with the letters Ы, Э, Ё and Ъ. Russian also appears rarely in Ukraine and eastern Estonia.

differs.how: Ukrainian has Є, Ґ, І, Ї instead

clues.title: Language: 'улица' means street
text: The Russian word for street is **улица** (ulitsa), sometimes abbreviated **ул.** (ul.).
NOTE: Bulgarian and most other Slavic languages also use улица / ulica. The Ukrainian word however is вулиця (vulytsya), abbreviated вул. (vul.).

images.caption: Street sign reading улица КРАСНОАРМЕЙСКАЯ, with a red circle enlarging the word улица

clues.summary: Street is улица, short ул. Bulgarian and most Slavic languages say something similar, but Ukrainian says вулиця.

clues.title: Language: 'город' means city
text: The Russian word for city is **город** (gorod), abbreviated **г.** (g.).
NOTE: The Ukrainian word is місто (misto), abbreviated м. (m.).

images.caption: Yellow shop sign reading МО г. КРАСНОДАР, with a circle enlarging the г. abbreviation for city

clues.summary: City is город, short г. Ukrainian says місто, short м.

clues.title: Bollard: three main types
text: Russia has three main types of bollards: a very thin type being attached to a stick, one with a black top section and a red vertical reflector below and a German-style bollard.
clues.summary: Three common bollards: a very thin one on a stick, one with a black top and a red vertical reflector below, and a German-style one.

clues.title: Roads: lots of bollards at intersections
text: Near intersections in Russia you will commonly see a very **large number of bollards**.
clues.summary: Intersections often have a very large number of bollards.

clues.title: Roads: unusually wide intersections
text: Along with containing a large number of bollards, many intersections are **unusually wide** compared to other countries.
clues.summary: Many intersections are unusually wide compared to other countries.

clues.title: Signposts: black painted bottoms
text: Signposts in Russia often have **black painted bottoms**.
NOTE: This is also common in Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: Signposts often have black painted bottoms. Common in Kazakhstan too.

clues.title: Pole: square concrete
text: Russia mainly uses **square concrete poles**.
NOTE: Square concrete poles can be seen in other post-Soviet countries, such as Ukraine, Lithuania, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan.

images.caption: A square concrete pole in the sky; the red circle zooms in on it, left

clues.summary: Mostly square concrete poles. Ukraine, Lithuania, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan have them too.

clues.title: Pole: concrete support blocks at the base
text: You can often see **concrete support blocks** at the bottom of utility poles, with wooden poles often being raised above ground by the support.

NOTE: [Similar blocks](https://www.google.com/maps/@48.4300351,17.7728644,3a,32.5y,3.03h,74.13t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sQ_utNdLPQAxCA1f1l0Jgnw!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu) are found in several Central and Eastern European countries.
clues.summary: Utility poles often have concrete support blocks at the bottom, with wooden poles often lifted off the ground by them. Several Central and Eastern European countries have similar blocks.

clues.title: Google car: black or white Gen 3, long antenna
text: Three Generation 3 Street View cars are commonly found in Russia. The two most useful ones for recognising Russia are a black and a [white](https://goo.gl/maps/MmC3SpuSmhV5ezux9) car, both with a long antenna. You may also see a [short antenna](https://goo.gl/maps/x1ryuJiJL9VjkEWx6) without a visible car.
NOTE: Short antenna without a visible car in Generation 3 is common in Europe. Both black and white cars with long antenna can show up in Generation 3 Europe, but are not as common.

images.caption: Car blurs labelled black car long antenna, white car long antenna and short antenna

clues.summary: Gen 3 mostly has a black or white car with a long antenna, or a short antenna with no visible car. Short antenna alone is common across Europe, and black or white long-antenna cars appear in Europe but less often.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, three stripes
text: Russian pedestrian signs have a simply drawn person and **three stripes**. Signs will commonly have a **bright yellow border**.
NOTE: Ukraine, Lithuania, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan use the same design.
clues.summary: Simple person with three stripes, often with a bright yellow border. Ukraine, Lithuania, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan use the same design.

clues.title: Road: crossings with white and yellow stripes
text: Russian pedestrian crossings contain alternating **white and yellow stripes**.
NOTE: This is also common in Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: Pedestrian crossings have alternating white and yellow stripes. Common in Kazakhstan too.

clues.title: Guardrail: black and white stripes
text: **Black and white striped guardrails**, kerbs and bridge barriers are common in russia.
clues.summary: Black-and-white striped guardrails, kerbs and bridge barriers are common.

clues.title: Houses: big plain concrete apartment blocks
text: The vast majority of urban housing in Russia are large rectangular apartment buildings made of simple concrete. [Newer buildings](https://goo.gl/maps/qSWTTiaLytipTyBd7) in wealthier areas appear more modern.
clues.summary: Most city housing is big rectangular concrete apartment blocks. Newer buildings in wealthier areas look more modern.

clues.title: Houses: basic wooden houses with metal roofs
text: Rural housing in Russia consists mostly of a **basic wooden structure** with metal roofs.
clues.summary: Rural housing is mostly basic wooden structures with metal roofs.

clues.title: Houses: richly decorated window frames, often blue
text: This style of **richly decorated window frames** is commonly found on traditional Russian homes, especially on log cabins. They are often painted blue.
clues.summary: Richly decorated window frames on traditional log cabins, often painted blue.

clues.title: Pipes: raised above ground on vertical pipes
text: In urban areas, you can sometimes see **pipes** which are exposed above the ground and are held up by other vertical pipes.
NOTE: This also occurs in Georgia and Ukraine, but in Ukraine it is less common.
clues.summary: In towns, pipes run exposed above ground, held up by vertical pipes. Georgia and Ukraine have this too, Ukraine less often.

clues.title: Pole: black-and-white striped shields on highways
text: **Black & white-striped pole shields** are common along highways, especially in European Russia.
clues.summary: Black-and-white striped shields on poles along highways, especially in the European part.

clues.title: Plants: white peeling birch bark
text: Birch trees, identified by their white peeling bark, have a wide range in Russia. Notably they are almost never found far south or far north in the western part of the country.
clues.summary: Birches have a wide range but almost never grow in the far south or far north in the west.

clues.title: Plants: birches packed tight, birch-only forests
text: Birches very close together, as well as forests consisting of **only birches**, are indicative of areas east of the Urals, most commonly between Chelyabinsk Oblast and Novosibirsk Oblast.
clues.summary: Birches very close together, and forests of only birch, mean east of the Urals, most common between two central Siberian regions.

clues.title: Plants: Siberian larch, needle leaves
text: Siberian larches are one of the dominant tree species in much of eastern Russia, recognized by their unique **needle-like leaves**. Generally speaking, they become more prevalent the further east you go in the country, as well as at high elevations.
clues.summary: Siberian larches dominate much of the east, with needle-like leaves. They become more common the further east and at high altitude.

clues.title: Plants: spruce, dark dense droopy branches
text: Spruce trees are an **evergreen tree** that can be identified by their dense and droopy or parallel branches, and generally are darker in color than most trees.
A similar evergreen tree, a [caucasian fir](https://maps.app.goo.gl/1XKsGPrBJaZiuSXn9), exists in the Caucasus Mountains. It has much more well organized and straighter branches.

NOTE: Larches have branches which point up and are less dense. Some [larches](https://maps.app.goo.gl/jmi4vRoWbfEr8TD37) can look very similar, but can be thought of as having much more unruly branches and look less “healthy”. Nonetheless, use with caution, especially on rounds that look eastern.
clues.summary: Spruce is evergreen, dark and dense with droopy or parallel branches. Caucasian fir has straighter, more orderly branches. Larches have upward, less dense, unruly branches and can look similar.

clues.title: Plants: giant butterbur, huge round leaves
text: [Giant butterbur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petasites_japonicus) (commonly referred to as Sakhalin cabbage) is very common in Sakhalin Oblast, particularly in the southern half. Related plants can very rarely be found in [Adygea](https://goo.gl/maps/wWv1UwyS1XfNpC4v6).
clues.summary: Giant butterbur ('Sakhalin cabbage') is very common on the Far East island, mostly in the south half. Related plants rarely appear near the Black Sea.

clues.title: Plants: tall white flower heads (hogweed)
text: This type of white flower ([heracleum sosnowskyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heracleum_sosnowskyi)) is most commonly found around Moscow, Komi Republic, and Perm Krai.
clues.summary: Tall white flowers of Sosnowsky's hogweed are most common around the capital, in the north-west Komi region and near the Urals.

clues.title: Plants: lots of pink fireweed
text: Large amounts of the pink or red flower fireweed ([Chamaenerion angustifolium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamaenerion_angustifolium)) typically indicates a northern region of Russia. Similarly, most places north of Moscow commonly have fireweed.
clues.summary: Large amounts of pink or red fireweed point to a northern region, and most places north of the capital have it.

clues.title: Plants: sunflowers near Ukraine and the Volga
text: **Sunflowers **are common along the border with Ukraine as well as more eastern oblasts like Ulyanovsk, Samara, and northern Orenburg.
clues.summary: Sunflowers are common along the Ukraine border and in eastern Volga-Urals regions.

clues.title: Plants: blue lupines
text: [Blue-pod lupines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupinus_polyphyllus) appear very commonly in northern Vladimir Oblast, eastern Ivanovo Oblast, and southwestern Kostroma Oblast. It can also be found less commonly elsewhere in Kirov Oblast and towards the Baltics.
clues.summary: Blue lupines are very common in a few regions north-east of the capital, less common in Kirov and toward the Baltics.

clues.title: Plants: black poplar near Ukraine and Kazakhstan
text: The **black poplar** is commonly found south, near the border with Ukraine, as well as toward the western border with Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: Black poplars are common in the south near Ukraine and toward Kazakhstan's border.

clues.title: Plants: Russian olive along the border
text: The [Russian olive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaeagnus_angustifolia) is typically found along the Kazakhstan border.
clues.summary: The Russian olive grows mostly along the Kazakhstan border.

clues.title: Plants: lined oaks with a white stripe
text: **Lined oak trees**, often with a single white stripe around the trunk, are extremely common in Kaliningrad.
clues.summary: Lined oak trees, often with a white stripe around the trunk, are extremely common in the western exclave.

clues.title: Plants: sparse planted larches, open fields
text: Sparsely **planted larches** along the road with open rolling fields is common in Tatarstan and adjacent federal subjects.
clues.summary: Sparsely planted larches along the road with open rolling fields are common in one Volga republic and nearby areas.

clues.title: Soil: sandy roadsides
text: **Sandy roadsides** are common in Khanty-Mansi and Yamalo-Nenets and adjacent subjects, as well as areas around [Nizhny Novgorod ](https://goo.gl/maps/NSDDrfNaFFCQPF8z5)on the Volga river. Other notable areas are [Karelia](https://goo.gl/maps/qw6yxjAp1TvUTT7S8), [Murmansk](https://goo.gl/maps/t4fzZ21q1MZrQLzG6), and [western Sakha](https://goo.gl/maps/QHWgEJ1kwRXxAEPu7). Beware, however, that sandy roadsides can less commonly be found near rivers in other regions.
clues.summary: Sandy roadsides are common in two western Siberian regions, near one Volga city, and in Karelia, the far north-west and western Sakha. They also appear near rivers elsewhere.

clues.title: Soil: red soil in highlighted areas
text: **Red soil** is common in the highlighted areas, notably around Izhevsk and Perm, much of Arkhangelsk Oblast, Leningrad Oblast, and Pskov Oblast, and near Volgograd and Astrakhan. Note that this map is by no means exhaustive; red soil can be found almost anywhere in the country near water or iron mines.
clues.summary: Red soil is common around several western regions and in the south-east. Red soil can appear almost anywhere near water or iron mines.

clues.title: Landscape: grey gravelly soil, many volcanoes
text: The Kamchatka peninsula has unique **grey gravelly soil**, as well as the largest number of **volcanoes** of any region in Russia. They are frequently seen across the peninsula, and in some places can appear quite close such as in [Klyuchi](https://goo.gl/maps/2JTY8XjBELQ2Q2tT8).
clues.summary: The Far East peninsula has grey gravelly soil and the most volcanoes in the country, often seen quite close.

clues.title: Soil: very gravelly dark soil near eastern mountains
text: Extremely gravelly and sometimes [dark](https://goo.gl/maps/DqAozgnTPiGBAj7g8) soil appears as you approach the mountains east of Yakutsk, starting around Keskil.
clues.summary: Extremely gravelly, sometimes dark soil approaches the mountains east of one far-eastern city.

clues.title: Landscape: lush hilly forests, overcast, white car
text: **Lush** and diverse forests in a **hilly** landscape characterises the noticeably warmer region around Vladivostok. Most of the coverage is overcast and has a white car with a long antenna. Further south, near the tri-border, you will find a more open [rolling hill landscape](https://goo.gl/maps/ErMpfen9KCE4HGHE7).
clues.summary: The warm south-east around the port city has lush mixed forests on hills, mostly overcast coverage with a white long-antenna car. Further south, a more open rolling landscape.

clues.title: Coverage: tall hazy hills, unpaved dark gravel road
text: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway going to Magadan features a lot of tall **hills** and **mountains**, usually shrouded in a **haze**. Most of the roads are unpaved and feature **dark gravelly soil**. The haze is not present in the western half.
clues.summary: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway has tall hills and mountains in haze, unpaved roads and dark gravelly soil. The west half has no haze.

clues.title: Road: larches, big mountains, Gen 4 white car
text: A presence of Siberian larches and large mountains on a mostly paved, but sometimes [wide-gravel road](https://goo.gl/maps/ztavuzTw3BXAyNMv6) indicates the main road south of Yakutsk, with [Generation 4 white car](https://goo.gl/maps/4VP2UsVh2FrsQjBg8) appearing north of Berkakit.
clues.summary: Siberian larches, large mountains and a mostly paved road, sometimes with wide gravel, mean the main road south of one far-eastern city. A Gen 4 white car appears further north.

clues.title: Coverage: very hazy, orange or white
text: Very **hazy coverage** is found east and south of Mirny, especially along the Vilyuy river. The colour of the haze varies, but it is often orange or [white](https://goo.gl/maps/QMfuHapbJnFYAyop6).
clues.summary: Very hazy coverage east and south of one diamond-mining town, especially along a river. Haze is often orange or white.

clues.title: Landscape: open grass, shrubs and mountains
text: The landscape in Buryatia is very unique, containing open grassy landscape with shrubs and mountains. It is lusher near Baikal, but the mountains persist.
clues.summary: Open grassy land with shrubs and mountains. Lusher near the big lake, but the mountains stay.

clues.title: Coverage: forest fire haze, open rolling land
text: This **forest fire haze** is found near Lake Gusinoye, southwest of Ulan-Ude in Buryatia. While similar to the haze found near [Mirny](https://maps.app.goo.gl/kZY7oWKZW3bHoFp5A), the Buryatia haze coverage can typically be recognised by the **open rolling landscape**, which is not found near Mirny.
clues.summary: Forest fire haze near a lake south-west of the republic capital. It resembles the haze near the diamond town but has an open rolling landscape.

clues.title: Google car: black car, long antenna, mountains and fog
text: The main road of Altai Republic has a black car long antenna driving north **through the Altai Mountains**, often with **foggy or rainy** coverage.
clues.summary: The main road of one southern mountain republic has a black long-antenna car driving north through mountains, often foggy or rainy.

clues.title: Landscape: dry steppe mountains, long antenna
text: **Dry steppe mountains** with a long antenna will usually indicate the Tuva Republic. The south part of the main road in the [Altai Republic](https://goo.gl/maps/C7aWe5KJWyT8Sa3W6) and Tuva can appear similarly dry, so things such as driving direction and cloudiness can be used to distinguish them.
clues.summary: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna usually mean one southern Siberian republic. The south of the neighbouring mountain republic's road looks similar, so use driving direction and clouds.

clues.title: Landscape: flat, very low vegetation, far north
text: The landscape in the far north can be recognised by the relatively **flat** landscape, with **very low vegetation**.
clues.summary: The far north is relatively flat with very low plants.

clues.title: Landscape: green farm fields with birch patches
text: The coverage in Omsk Oblast is some of the most recognizable in Russia. It is typically summer Generation 4 and has a distinct landscape consisting of green agricultural fields, which are interrupted by isolated patches of (primarily) birch forest.
Note that in Generation 3, this landscape can be seen in a much larger area of Russia.
NOTE: This combination of coverage and landscape spills over slightly into the neighbouring Tyumen and Novosibirsk Oblasts (in the south, and near Tatarsk, respectively).
clues.summary: One Siberian region's summer Gen 4 shows green farm fields interrupted by isolated patches of birch forest. In Gen 3 this landscape covers a much larger area.

clues.title: Landscape: extremely dry and flat
text: The area west of the Caspian Sea can often be recognised by its extremely **dry and flat landscape**, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan Oblast, and Dagestan.
clues.summary: The area west of the Caspian Sea is extremely dry and flat, especially in the three regions there.

clues.title: Landscape: grass and bushes, early spring Gen 4
text: **Grassy fields**, with **bushy vegetation**, in early spring Generation 4 coverage is typical for Dagestan. The landscape can either be completely [flat](https://goo.gl/maps/aagmDRf8TAcokMkn9) or [mountainous](https://goo.gl/maps/ZbWrv4FiuSGLBzHq9). [These flowers](https://maps.app.goo.gl/P26tJd6Lf73upk4G8) are also quite common in the Generation 4 Dagestan coverage.
clues.summary: Grassy fields with bushes in early spring Gen 4, either flat or mountainous, with common small flowers, point to one Caucasus republic.

clues.title: Landscape: Caucasus mountains, highest peak
text: The **Caucasus mountain range** is one of the largest mountain ranges in Russia. The tallest mountain in Russia, [Mount Elbrus](https://goo.gl/maps/v1yAcshzeyBme85y8), can be found on the border of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic and Karachay-Cherkessia.
clues.summary: The Caucasus is one of the biggest ranges, with the tallest mountain in the country on the border of two republics.

clues.title: Landscape: rocks along the road
text: **Rocks** along the road are extremely common throughout most of Karelia and Murmansk Oblast. They can also be found in Perm Krai and Buryatia but are less common and smaller in size.
clues.summary: Rocks along the road are extremely common in the north-west, and smaller and rarer in the Urals and near the big Siberian lake.

clues.title: Landscape: open hills, low shrubs, fireweed
text: An open, hilly landscape with low shrubbery and [fireweed](https://goo.gl/maps/jQxpJeqbas286g7i7) usually indicates Murmansk. The lower the shrubbery, the more north it generally is.
clues.summary: Open hilly land with low shrubs and fireweed usually means the far north-west. The lower the shrubs, the further north.

clues.title: Phone numbers: area code first digit shows region
text: This is a map of Russian **area codes**. Notably, area codes starting with 8 are in the west, codes starting with 3 are fairly central and codes starting with 4 are either east or around Moscow.
clues.summary: Area codes starting with 8 are in the west, 3 fairly central, and 4 either east or around the capital.

clues.title: Plates: regional code on the right
text: In Generation 3 coverage you will somewhat commonly find unblurred licence plates, featuring a **regional code** on the right side. The codes are generally ordered alphabetically within each [type of federal subject](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_subjects_of_Russia#Types), starting at republics and ending with autonomous okrugs. Therefore, the [Republic of Adygea](https://maps.app.goo.gl/PhX9zVnMQfBCvHQi7) will be represented by 01, and the [Amur Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/AXNwmSJ1vio1pRCo7) by 28, both being the first alphabetical subjects of republics and oblasts respectively. If you encounter a [three digit code](https://maps.app.goo.gl/BiQGFQEG51Xxc7fc7), the second and third digit will form the regional code, in this case 123 becomes 23, for Krasnodar Krai. You may also find the codes written out on the back of [trucks](https://maps.app.goo.gl/NVQNyKpSUXZ3i4LG6) and [vans](https://www.google.com/maps/@56.6511783,66.3012014,3a,15y,5.71h,78.8t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s8nSDptPKXAhrtGZE6nzskg!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: In Gen 3 you sometimes see unblurred plates with a regional code on the right, ordered alphabetically within each type of region, so 01 is the first republic and 28 an oblast. Three-digit codes add extra regions.

clues.title: Bus stops: shelters unique to regions
text: These are the bus stops unique to specific federal subjects in Russia. Notably common and memorable ones include Krasnoyarsk Krai, Chuvashia, Tatarstan, and Mari El Republic.
clues.summary: Some federal regions have bus stops that are unique to them. Notable ones are in a Siberian territory and three Volga republics.

clues.title: Cars: right-hand-drive Japanese cars in the east
text: Japanese-made cars with the **steering wheel on the right** become more common the further east you go, generally starting around Novosibirsk.
clues.summary: Right-hand-drive Japanese-made cars become more common going east, starting around the big Siberian city.

clues.title: Bollard: very thin one on a stick, east
text: Russian bollards that appear very thin and attached to a stick are usually found in the eastern part of the country, starting around Omsk. Note that [ordinary Russian bollards](https://goo.gl/maps/RnBNJE9kGwChsj9G7) are still plentiful in this part of the country.
clues.summary: The very thin bollard on a stick is usually in the east, starting around one Siberian city. Ordinary bollards remain plentiful there.

clues.title: Signs: black sign bottoms in the south
text: This **black traffic sign bottom** is primarily found in Stavropol and Chechnya, as well as western Dagestan. Rarely, exceptions can be found in other southern federal subjects such as [Kabardino Balkaria](https://goo.gl/maps/XeKf78CHzYCEtTQX8), but these will typically be uncolored.
clues.summary: Black sign bottoms are mostly in two southern regions and west Dagestan. Rare exceptions in other southern regions are usually uncoloured.

clues.title: Signposts: clips on the edges
text: **Clips** on edges of signposts are found in Leningrad and St. Petersburg, and very rarely in Pskov, Novgorod or elsewhere.
clues.summary: Clips on the edges of signposts are found around the north-west big city and its region, very rarely in neighbouring ones.

clues.title: Road lines: outer dashed lines
text: **Outer dashed road lines** are usually found throughout Kursk Oblast. An exception can be found in [Tuva Republic](https://goo.gl/maps/h6GYSQrhjBXDWJD39). Rarer exceptions include [the Republic of Karelia](https://goo.gl/maps/PvQvkaH63nHGqvD17), [Primorsky Krai](https://goo.gl/maps/6pXTrSNjaNmVToYF8) and [Khabarovsk Krai](https://goo.gl/maps/34mpJJfXMNBqKnJm9).
clues.summary: Outer dashed lines are usual in one south-western region. Exceptions in a Siberian republic and, rarely, in the north-west and Far East.

clues.title: Roads: concrete block roads in the far north
text: As you go further north in Russia, some roads are made out of several **concrete blocks**. It is notably common in the Komi Republic, Nenets, and Yamalo-Nenets.
clues.summary: Further north, some roads are made of several concrete blocks, especially in the Komi region and two Arctic districts.

clues.title: Language: bilingual signs in two Volga republics
text: Some republics of Russia with minority languages use bilingual town entry and directional signs, such as in Bashkortostan and Tatarstan displaying Bashkir and Tatar respectively.
clues.summary: Town entry and direction signs show Bashkir or Tatar alongside Russian in the two republics.

clues.title: Language: town names in Cyrillic and Latin
text: **Town names** written in both the Cyrillic and **Latin** alphabets are common near the Baltic border and around Moscow, and to a lesser extent in federal subjects on the Finnish border.
clues.summary: Town names in both Cyrillic and Latin are common near the Baltic border, around the capital and, less so, near Finland.

clues.title: Signs: brown tourist attraction signs
text: These **brown signs**, pointing to typical tourist attractions, are common in Moscow Oblast and the oblasts bordering it. However, they can also less commonly be seen in city centres or near tourist attractions of [other regions](https://www.google.com/maps/@61.821949,34.3074923,3a,17.8y,22.25h,94.58t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1stZhKu0HYudsYXdctQ9_AyQ!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: Brown signs pointing to tourist attractions are common around the capital and its neighbouring regions, and less often in city centres elsewhere.

clues.title: Houses: white limestone brick
text: Buildings made of **white limestone brick** are indicative of Dagestan, as well as adjacent regions.
NOTE: Brick architecture is more consistent the more brick structures you can see in the round.
clues.summary: White limestone brick buildings point to one southern republic and adjacent regions. Works better the more brick buildings you see.

clues.title: Houses: almost entirely red brick
text: Buildings made almost entirely of **red brick** are mostly found in the south, with Magnitogorsk, Orsk, and Omsk being notable exceptions.
NOTE: This clue is more consistent the more brick structures you can see in the round.
clues.summary: Almost entirely red brick buildings are mostly in the south, with three industrial cities as exceptions. Works better the more brick you see.

clues.title: Mosques: common in the south and two Volga republics
text: While mosques can be found everywhere in Russia, they are by far most common in areas with a Muslim majority, mainly in much of south Russia as well as Tatarstan and Bashkortostan.
clues.summary: Mosques appear everywhere but are far more common in areas with a Muslim majority: much of the south and two Volga republics.

clues.title: Houses: green roofs, red brick with white stone
text: Historical buildings in Mari El often have a unique architecture style. You will frequently see design patterns that include **green roofs**, red brick sprinkled with white stone details. [Local churches](https://www.google.com/maps/@56.2884468,46.2917123,3a,42.4y,279.05h,107.04t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1s5uTfNmrvJwCTQn0915srvw!2e0!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fpanoid%3D5uTfNmrvJwCTQn0915srvw%26cb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile.gps%26w%3D203%26h%3D100%26yaw%3D9.734652%26pitch%3D0%26thumbfov%3D100!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) commonly feature a similar style.
clues.summary: Historic buildings in one Volga republic often have green roofs and red brick with white stone details. Local churches share the style.

clues.title: Coverage: map of coverage, sparse in east and north
text: This is the full coverage map of Russia. It can be helpful to know areas where there isn’t any coverage. The coverage is notably very sparse in the east and north.
You can check out the extent of the official coverage[ on this website](https://sv-map.netlify.app/#base=roadmap&cov=official&zoom=4&center=63.09475846224108%2C101.77734375000001).
clues.summary: The coverage map shows large gaps. Coverage is very sparse in the east and north.

clues.title: Google car: white long-antenna car
text: [White car long antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/szUNXBWMYPjJ6jMA6) is found in many places, most commonly in [southern Chelyabinsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/u2ofsEtYhTK1kxpr9), on [snow coverage around Novosibirsk](https://goo.gl/maps/WT1mwvr1mZH9Nsy88), and in the [Far East](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UcNfar31Lf4yD8pD7) beginning in [Amur Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/uJivjvnTnNdf4LHq5).

NOTE: While [Kamchatka](https://goo.gl/maps/vbKvMrHXtE7anj636) technically has a silver car (with a B type antenna), it often appears white and is part of the small group of exceptions to black and white.
clues.summary: The white long-antenna car appears in southern Chelyabinsk, in snow coverage around one Siberian city and in the Far East from Amur Oblast on. Kamchatka's silver car often looks white.

clues.title: Google car: A-type short antenna, high ridge right
text: The [A-type short antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/13hZAJw2TiAoyFP17) has its highest ridge on the right. Notable areas for this antenna are around [Kaluga](https://maps.app.goo.gl/JvchV2vn13QwiTG57), [Orenburg](https://maps.app.goo.gl/nYa3htnmJtm9RUEc9), and [Krasnodar](https://maps.app.goo.gl/48JHYVMTGEwN7XCu8).
clues.summary: The A-type short antenna has its highest ridge on the right. Notable around Kaluga, Orenburg and Krasnodar.

clues.title: Google car: B-type short antenna, high ridge left
text: The [B-type short antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/otoKbscwAem4eCh89) has its highest ridge on the left. This antenna is wide-ranging, but it is most notably found near [Nizhny Novgorod](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6nmWkEgaUkHRydZt5), [Elista](https://maps.app.goo.gl/sb6XLo7VMBzFQiiu8), and [Yekaterinburg](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3VHAgPgQ6EWcbjys8) and [Tyumen](https://maps.app.goo.gl/rcYGf1PeEnWmD1Sc6).
clues.summary: The B-type short antenna has its highest ridge on the left. Wide-ranging, but notable near Nizhny Novgorod, Elista, Yekaterinburg and Tyumen.

clues.title: Google car: B-type antenna with rectangular ridge
text: The [B-type pronounced antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/WwzMFjRSbmQUgBHB9) is the same as the B-type antenna but the ridge is more “rectangular”. This antenna is fairly limited, only being found commonly in [Moscow Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tziG6gD8RNd8ByJN8), [Kurgan Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HMFY2AUsYsPMmEFm6), [near Krasnoyarsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Wv94BFV16DXcfnVx6), and [southwest Krasnodar](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9hM7GWG3Mk7AazpJ7).
clues.summary: Like the B-type but with a more rectangular ridge. Common near Moscow, Kurgan, Krasnoyarsk and south-west Krasnodar.

clues.title: Google car: C-type short antenna, low twisting ridges
text: The [C-type short antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/7WisPoWqAk3itE7eA) can be thought of as a low A-type or a “twisting antenna” with the ridges being further from the top. It is found [north](https://maps.app.goo.gl/snkxCqnaS1bZc1hY9) and [east](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6gMAwy8bad7C9J2dA) of Moscow, with the furthest south being [Rostov Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/GjFfAVgNQaRzLKkL7).
clues.summary: A low A-type or twisting antenna with the ridges further from the top. Found north and east of the capital, furthest south in Rostov Oblast.

clues.title: Google car: blurrier short antenna
text: The [blurred short antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8uWV4EHvPCH1dZKUA) is visibly blurrier than any of the other short antennas. It is mainly found in two major clusters around [Ufa](https://maps.app.goo.gl/rgZgng4EcRjznQuP6) and from [Stavropol](https://maps.app.goo.gl/7d5Q8kbPNPQPDMuGA) to [Makhachkala](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ujH4F6CZZc3qeSRN7).
clues.summary: A short antenna that is visibly blurrier than the other types. Two clusters: around Ufa, and from Stavropol to Makhachkala.

clues.title: Google car: A-type long antenna, high ridge right
text: The [A-type long antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/PuGiesP9DAUdSiRKA) has its highest ridge on the right side. Notable areas include [Leningrad Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/4GDjJxHqF2cerU1RA), [Republic of Karelia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/MN3ZHGme7BvopS7h9), and [Vologda Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/KRnogy4K1mUbL9y99). Almost all the white car long antenna coverage is A-type, so checking for A-type can also help confirm car colour.
clues.summary: The A-type long antenna has its highest ridge on the right. Notable in the north-west. Almost all white long-antenna cars are A-type.

clues.title: Google car: B-type long antenna, high ridge left
text: The [B-type long antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/xiJHmjsXcMQyQZ1d9) has its highest ridge on the left side. Notable areas include [Yaroslav](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZdC9XJiP3NKKA9QA6) to [Vladimir](https://maps.app.goo.gl/wEscjWspwirDVd696), [Tula Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ajNom88LdYrKfRAX6), and much of the coverage near [Tuva](https://maps.app.goo.gl/icUb6qp4Y8MzFd2P7) and [Irkutsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UmZN7hTvhWZv6yKk8).

NOTE: There are two other long antenna types, referred to as [CA](https://maps.app.goo.gl/eMwfHi2kLMyXc8u27) and [CB](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tDHKLKq8ENnxfWKEA), but due to their relative lack of usefulness they will not be covered here.
clues.summary: The B-type long antenna has its highest ridge on the left. Notable from Yaroslavl to Vladimir, Tula Oblast and around Tuva and Irkutsk.

clues.title: Google car: blurrier long-antenna car
text: [Blurred long antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/uqSetFHbhpcz8xoy9) is visibly blurrier than other long antenna cars, and is a strong clue for [Sakhalin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/NZW6zaBoyGu7Wn6u7) and [various](https://maps.app.goo.gl/zcueGiDZjMNgD5PZA) [roads](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UyHPvXwew65N9W1C8) in the east, as well as much of [Khanty-Mansi](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Vpwb7fPXkVYdxHmYA). On the other end there exists a blurred antenna in far western [Bryansk Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/nKJyHgpuCi95BtWu7) and some of [Tula Oblast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/44N5R9CyPjxWu2RL9).
clues.summary: A long antenna that is visibly blurrier than others: strong for Sakhalin, roads in the east and much of Khanty-Mansi, but also in far west Bryansk and some of Tula.

clues.title: Google car: short antenna tilted left
text: The [tilted short antenna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9dsW6TyNZJ1vTVo69) is visibly tilted to the left and can be found primarily on a diagonal from [St. Petersburg](https://maps.app.goo.gl/uYJumDRfPtDcYF8i7) down to [Volgograd](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HcLrcfJw396hVA3k6), with exceptions in [Stavropol](https://maps.app.goo.gl/xnVy4Amy7TYgydFG6) and [Ufa.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3ndyQtC4AoWqDXns5) Since the ridge is on the same side, it can sometimes appear as the A-type short antenna.
clues.summary: A short antenna visibly tilted to the left, mostly on a diagonal from St. Petersburg to Volgograd, with exceptions around Stavropol and Ufa. It can look like the A-type.

clues.title: Google car: large red brake light
text: A large, red brake light is common in Kaliningrad, however it can also be found in some [older coverage](https://goo.gl/maps/bms7QA2bzAr5VLBX8) in western Russia.
clues.summary: A large red brake light is common in the western exclave, and appears in some older western coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: autumn Gen 3 in the west
text: Autumn Generation 3 coverage is common in Kaliningrad, Bryansk, Tula, and Belgorod in western Russia, but Kaliningrad only has autumn coverage.
clues.summary: Autumn Gen 3 is common in the western exclave, Bryansk, Tula and Belgorod, but the exclave only has autumn coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: lots of snow on the ground in Gen 4
text: In Generation 4 coverage, **significant snow on the ground** is most commonly seen in Saratov Oblast and Eastern Voronezh Oblast.
clues.summary: Gen 4 with plenty of snow on the ground is most common in Saratov and eastern Voronezh.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 widespread, not Altai or Far East
text: **Generation 4** coverage is quite extensive and is found in most federal subjects in the country. Notably, areas like the Altai mountains and most of the Far East lack Generation 4 completely. Knowing where Generation 4 can be found isn’t the most helpful at the beginner level; other clues like season and car are more important. The dark red signifies areas where all of the coverage is Generation 4.
clues.summary: Gen 4 is found in most regions. The Altai mountains and most of the Far East have none. Season and car matter more than this at a beginner level.

clues.title: Coverage: winter Gen 4 in the south
text: [Winter Generation 4](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tKFTbt1t6mYGmF1CA) is most common in the south of Russia, ranging from [Ryazan](https://www.google.com/maps/@54.521468,41.2920492,3a,75y,136.68h,90.82t,1.58r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s8GGSJc8bRgrChfct0st5lg!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu) all the way down to [Kabardino-Balkaria](https://maps.app.goo.gl/sqbQHZkc1aXttg8G9) and [Dagestan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/eSpNpPM7VYWquBPN7). Winter can appear differently depending on the month (and even time of month the coverage was taken) which can be used to further regionguess.
clues.summary: Winter Gen 4 is most common in the south, from Ryazan down to Kabardino-Balkaria and Dagestan. Its look varies by month.

clues.title: Coverage: spring Gen 4 in a few places
text: [Spring Generation 4](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mxR9jx12qcpoqiX47) is common in several distinct places, such as around [Kemerovo](https://maps.app.goo.gl/AYpeDSAXjY4DTcfHA) and [Krasnoyarsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6XmSQBo12yhE4peS7), [Orenburg](https://maps.app.goo.gl/gGk8Qr7GFamJkEUj9) and [Kamyshin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Xzo5rBpi1mDngfmw7), around [Lipetsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/5rDYMi3imMh6wZ9S6), and in [Moscow city](https://maps.app.goo.gl/CzcoMF9KbXZqerCWA). Differentiating these places typically comes down to landscape, as they tend to be fairly distinct.
clues.summary: Spring Gen 4 is common around Kemerovo, Krasnoyarsk, Orenburg, Kamyshin, Lipetsk and Moscow city. Landscape tells these apart.

clues.title: Coverage: summer Gen 4
text: [Summer Generation 4](https://maps.app.goo.gl/87VXQczGm3HeChX18) is the most common coverage in generation 4. It is pretty much everywhere except in the south and some of the east, but can be further subdivided by car colour.
clues.summary: Summer Gen 4 is the most common Gen 4 coverage, almost everywhere except the south and parts of the east. Car colour helps divide it.

clues.title: Coverage: autumn Gen 4, rare
text: [Autumn Generation 4](https://maps.app.goo.gl/4ePdHYjvkycsZWMP6) is quite rare and only found around [Kazan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/CuYMZ5RFdFKH4CFX7) and a few roads in [Murmansk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/FVbne7gzizSc2mdu8), as well as some of [Ulan-Ude](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cGxwLd6k866DgMRr9).
clues.summary: Autumn Gen 4 is rare: around Kazan, a few roads in the far north-west and part of Ulan-Ude.

clues.title: Google car: red Gen 4 car
text: [Generation 4 red car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/XZNnHtvtZbyWYqt99) is the most common generation 4 car meta, found primarily east around [Khanty-Mansi](https://maps.app.goo.gl/urkHYCZryyhY8kxdA), as well as along the main highways down to [Irkutsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/xm2khKQjsmjipnq9A) and [Ulan-Ude](https://maps.app.goo.gl/camcQ4mEZpFN61Um9). There is also a sizable patch near [Penza](https://maps.app.goo.gl/V1cagu4DLNtD9pGq5) and [Tatarstan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/vitVoMssWGjKgixL6), as well as [Rostov-on-Don](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YCTYFcj5NZ1efTRN9).
clues.summary: The most common Gen 4 car: mainly in the east around Khanty-Mansi and along main highways to Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude, with patches near Penza, Tatarstan and Rostov-on-Don.

clues.title: Google car: white Gen 4 car
text: [Generation 4 white car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ysyGKt4TvtWbGAHC7) is found in the May coverage near [Lipetsk](https://maps.app.goo.gl/FS32oVQjxE4G5bu57), in [Moscow city](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YtkYaj1V3t1P5nqk9), and most notably across all the coverage north of Berkatit in the [Sakha Republic](https://maps.app.goo.gl/vE7pUiAVqX3rvTAg7) and [Magadan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/AGFGntoW6UFFcPm79).
clues.summary: Gen 4 white car: May coverage near Lipetsk, in Moscow city, and across all coverage north of Berkakit in Sakha and in Magadan.

clues.title: Google car: black Gen 4 car
text: [Generation 4 black car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hV1BDavTfgWjBezk8) is found mostly near [Moscow](https://maps.app.goo.gl/d3GSjMCXAaZiwfBp9), [Tver](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UqwBFR7gry7wDpZy9), and [Voronezh](https://maps.app.goo.gl/p5YktDMBB7Mksd8SA), with some also existing in [Tatarstan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/w6tJLmTsuvTsMHvJ6) and less commonly in the south.
clues.summary: Gen 4 black car: mostly near Moscow, Tver and Voronezh, some in Tatarstan and less often in the south.

clues.title: Coverage: dead winter, raised apartment blocks
text: Vorkuta in far northern Komi Republic has **dead-looking winter coverage**, sometimes with reddish soil. The apartment blocks will typically have large [northern apartment block foundations](https://goo.gl/maps/cUdFrbUXmuiUCWyE9).
clues.summary: A far northern mining town in winter, with dead-looking surroundings, sometimes reddish soil, and apartment blocks on large raised foundations.

clues.title: Coverage: winter at two Far East port towns
text: Sovetskaya Gavan and Vanino in eastern Khabarovsk have winter coverage, somewhat similar to Vorkuta.
NOTE: While Vorkuta and Vanino have similar coverage types, Vorkuta is noticeably flatter, having lower vegetation and a more barren landscape.
clues.summary: Two eastern port towns have winter coverage similar to the far northern one, but are less flat and barren, with more plants.

clues.title: Road: unpaved sandy road, stunted bushes
text: The road to Okha in northern Sakhalin is unpaved, revealing its very **sandy soil**. The road is surrounded by **short, stunted bushes and trees**.
clues.summary: The road to the northern island town is unpaved, very sandy, surrounded by short stunted bushes and trees.

clues.title: Road: mountains, sunny, black car with blurred antenna
text: The Khabarovsk-Vanino road has a **mountainous landscape** with very **sunny coverage**. It also drives west with a black car with a blurred, long antenna, which helps to confirm.
clues.summary: A mountainous road in sunny coverage driving west, with a black car with a blurred long antenna.

clues.title: Coverage: one road, rainy and foggy in the west
text: The Jewish Autonomous Oblast effectively has one road of coverage, outside of Birobidzhan. The west side has highly **rainy and foggy** coverage.
clues.summary: A small Far East region has basically one road of coverage apart from its capital. The west side is very rainy and foggy.

clues.title: Coverage: wet after rain, east side
text: On the east side of the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, the coverage turns from rainy to **wet** after the rain.
clues.summary: On the east side of that region, the coverage changes from rainy to wet after rain.

clues.title: Coverage: sunset, eastern landscape
text: **Sunset coverage**, with the sun very close to the horizon, with an eastern-looking landscape will be the P-297 in Amur Oblast, roughly between the towns of Never and Sivaki.
clues.summary: Sunset coverage with the sun very close to the horizon and an eastern landscape is road P-297, between two Far East towns.

clues.title: Landscape: sandy hills at sunset, big lake
text: Olkhon Island on Lake Baikal has a single road, driving on rolling **sandy hills during sunset**. You can often see Lake Baikal directly with a mountain ridge across the bay.
clues.summary: An island in the big Siberian lake has a single road over rolling sandy hills at sunset, often showing the lake and a mountain ridge across the bay.

clues.title: Landscape: green river basin, jagged mountains north
text: Tunkinsky National Park in western Buryatia is a very green **river basin** with tall, **jagged mountains** to the north. In comparison to most of Buryatia, it is much greener.
clues.summary: A national park in western Buryatia is a very green river basin with tall jagged mountains to the north, much greener than most of the republic.

clues.title: Coverage: flat desert, dirt tracks, Gen 4
text: In the desert-like region west of the Caspian Sea, this completely flat and rural Generation 4 coverage on small poorly-tracked dirt roads can only be found in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan Oblast.
clues.summary: Completely flat rural Gen 4 on small, poorly tracked dirt roads in the desert west of the Caspian Sea, only in northern Dagestan and south-west Astrakhan.

clues.title: Plants: palm trees on the Black Sea
text: **Tropical plants** in Russia such as palm trees are only found on the Black Sea, most commonly around Sochi.
clues.summary: Tropical plants such as palms only grow on the Black Sea coast, most around Sochi.

clues.title: Coverage: trekkers mostly on the Far East peninsula
text: Kamchatka trekkers encompass a majority of the trekkers present in Russia. They can be recognized using the same clues to recognize Kamchatka normally.
clues.summary: Most trekkers in the country are on the volcano peninsula, recognisable the same way as the peninsula itself.

clues.title: Sign: blue sign with English translations
text: These blue signs are only found in Moscow and usually feature **English translations** of important tourist points.
clues.summary: Blue signs with English translations of tourist points are only in the capital.

clues.title: Street sign: transliteration on black
text: St. Petersburg street signs include a **transliteration** of the street name on a black background. They are primarily found downtown.
clues.summary: Street signs include a Latin transliteration on a black background, mostly downtown in the northern big city.

clues.title: Street sign: circular with up to 4 languages
text: Saransk has an exclusive circular street sign design with the street name being written in up to **4 different languages**.
clues.summary: One Volga republic's capital has an exclusive circular street sign with the name in up to four languages.

clues.title: Language: Tatar signs say 'урамы'
text: **Tatar bilingual signs** use “урамы” (ур., abbreviated) for street instead of “улица” and are unsurprisingly found in Tatarstan.
clues.summary: Tatar bilingual signs use урамы (short ур.) for street instead of улица, found in Tatarstan.

clues.title: Language: Bashkir signs say 'урамы'
text: **Bashkir bilingual signs** are found in Bashkortostan and use “урамы” for street, the same as Tatar, but are often not abbreviated.
clues.summary: Bashkir bilingual signs also use урамы for street, but often not abbreviated.

clues.title: Language: Chuvash signs say 'урамӗ'
text: **Chuvash bilingual signs**, found in Chuvashia, use “урамӗ” for street.
clues.summary: Chuvash bilingual signs use урамӗ for street.

clues.title: Language: Mari signs say 'урем'
text: **Mari bilingual signs**, found in Mari El, use “урем” for street.
clues.summary: Mari bilingual signs use урем for street.

clues.title: Language: Komi signs say 'улича'
text: **Komi bilingual signs**, found in the Komi Republic, use “улича” for street.
clues.summary: Komi bilingual signs use улича for street.

clues.title: Pole: alternating red and white
text: These **alternating red and white** poles are mainly found in Ulyanovsk city, but also less commonly in the [greater Nizhny Novgorod area](https://goo.gl/maps/JNLBV3L6cogEaBiCA) as well as somewhat randomly elsewhere in the country.
clues.summary: Alternating red and white poles are mainly in one Volga city, less often around another and randomly elsewhere.

clues.title: Pole: striped red and white
text: These **striped red and white** poles are found mostly in Saransk, but also in a few other cities in Mordovia.
clues.summary: Striped red and white poles are mostly in one republic capital and a few other towns of that republic.

clues.title: Pole: yellow plates on a metal band
text: **Yellow pole plates** attached by a **metal band** are commonly found in Tatarstan. They are found on the majority of poles, but not all.

images.caption: Pole in a field; the red circle zooms in on yellow plates on a metal band

clues.summary: Yellow pole plates attached with a metal band are common in one Volga republic, on most but not all poles.

clues.title: Signposts: two yellow bands
text: On the main road of Murmansk in generation 4, as well as some roads in Karelia covered in 2018, the vast majority of signposts will have **two yellow bands** wrapped around them.

images.caption: Red circle zooms in on a roadside pole with two yellow bands

clues.summary: On the main road of the far north-west city in Gen 4, and some roads in Karelia from 2018, most signposts have two yellow bands.

clues.title: Roads: cobblestone pavement
text: **Cobblestone pavement** is notably common in [Kaliningrad](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cAtPVWR2WxLiyS8V8), [Nizhny Tagil](https://maps.app.goo.gl/iUD3LBhJYxSxdHFeA) in Sverdlovsk, and [Kizel](https://goo.gl/maps/2rLUZD6Rvei7qWwXA) in Perm Krai.
clues.summary: Cobblestone pavement is notably common in the western exclave, one Urals industrial town and one in the Perm region.

clues.title: Pole: extended insulator bars
text: **Extended insulator bars** on poles are notably found in southern Chelyabinsk Oblast and [eastern Orenburg Oblast](https://goo.gl/maps/ahe7wDESrVMJiZDD6), as well as [southern Kemerovo Oblast](https://goo.gl/maps/nSDobcgFvaTL8EPt5).
clues.summary: Extended insulator bars on poles, notably in southern Chelyabinsk, eastern Orenburg and southern Kemerovo.

clues.title: Pole: mesh-framework utility poles
text: Utility poles with a **mesh framework** are usually found in Petrozavodsk, but can much less commonly be found in cities like [Tolyatti](https://goo.gl/maps/QeRuT92WeXEavqv48).

images.caption: A mesh-framework utility pole on a lawn

clues.summary: Utility poles with a mesh framework are usually in Petrozavodsk, much less often in cities like Tolyatti.

clues.title: Pole: painted red
text: These **red painted** poles are only found in Murom.
clues.summary: Red painted poles are only in Murom.

clues.title: Pole: angled extended insulator bar
text: An **angled extended insulator bar** on the pole as shown is found in Chita.
clues.summary: An angled, extended insulator bar on the pole is found in Chita.

clues.title: Bollard: grey rectangle with two red reflectors
text: This unique bollard, with a **grey rectangle** and **double red reflectors**, is specific to the P100 in Kostroma Oblast.

images.caption: Thin pole on a roadside; the red circle at top left magnifies another pole with red reflectors

clues.summary: A unique bollard with a grey rectangle and two red reflectors, only on the P100 in Kostroma Oblast.
